html:
Baruch Spinoza was a philosopher born in Amsterdam in 1632 to a family of Portuguese Jews who had fled the Inquisition. He is one of the great thinkers of modern philosophy.

In 1656 the Jewish community of Amsterdam expelled him for his ideas. He earned his living grinding lenses. In his Ethics, set out like geometry, he argued that God and nature are one, that everything follows necessary laws, and that freedom comes from understanding. His Theological Political Treatise of 1670 read the Bible as a historical book and defended freedom of thought.

His books were banned even in the tolerant Dutch Republic, and the Ethics was published only after his death in 1677. Condemned as an atheist for a century, he became a hero of the radical Enlightenment. Einstein said he believed in Spinoza's God. See the Netherlands.
